/blog/ssd-transfer-time-advertised-speed.title: SSD transfer time: why the advertised MB/s is not your copy speed
/blog/ssd-transfer-time-advertised-speed.description: Estimate a transfer with the amount of data and a realistic end-to-end rate. An SSD’s advertised sequential read figure describes a particular test; it does not establish how quickly your source, destination, connection and files will complete a copy.

image.alt: Decision diagram for SSD transfer time: why the advertised MB/s is not your copy speed

/blog/new-pc-no-display-safe-checks/.title: A new PC has no display: read debug LEDs without guessing the faulty part
/blog/new-pc-no-display-safe-checks/.description: A persistent diagnostic LED helps choose an investigation path. It is not enough, by itself, to justify buying a replacement CPU, memory kit or GPU. Record the exact board and symptom, check the display path, then follow the manufacturer’s safe steps one change at a time.

image.alt: Decision diagram for A new PC has no display: read debug LEDs without guessing the faulty part

/blog/how-to-choose-gaming-ram/.title: RAM compatibility: read the exact kit, slots and QVL evidence
/blog/how-to-choose-gaming-ram/.description: A QVL records tested memory configurations. A missing entry is a missing validation record, not automatic proof that the kit cannot work. Match generation, kit part number, CPU platform, module count and board instructions before deciding what is supported and what still needs verification.

image.alt: Decision diagram for RAM compatibility: read the exact kit, slots and QVL evidence

/blog/choose-display-target-game-evidenc.title: Choose a monitor target: verify the output path, refresh rate and game evidence
/blog/choose-display-target-game-evidenc.description: Check three different questions: whether the display connection supports the intended mode, whether the operating system is using it, and whether the game can produce useful frames at your chosen settings. A monitor’s maximum refresh rate answers none of the other questions on its own.

image.alt: Decision diagram for Choose a monitor target: verify the output path, refresh rate and game evidence

/blog/will-a-graphics-card-fit-my-case/.title: Will this graphics card fit? Read the exact partner model and installed layout
/blog/will-a-graphics-card-fit-my-case/.description: Use the full partner-card model and the case’s allowance for the layout you will actually install. Check length, thickness, height, connection clearance and nearby hardware separately. A matching GPU chip name or a plausible 3D scene cannot prove physical fit.

image.alt: Decision diagram for Will this graphics card fit? Read the exact partner model and installed layout

/compare/rx-9070-vs-rx-9070-xt/.title: RX 9070 vs RX 9070 XT: specifications, power and the price decision
/compare/rx-9070-vs-rx-9070-xt/.description: Both designs list 16 GB of GDDR6, but the XT has more compute units and a higher typical board-power specification. Choose between exact partner cards using the games, installed layout and complete cost you can document. This comparison supplies no invented gaming average or universal winner.

image.alt: Decision diagram for RX 9070 vs RX 9070 XT: specifications, power and the price decision

/blog/ram-timings-cas-trcd-trp/.title: DDR5-6000 CL30 vs CL36: what the 2 ns calculation can tell you
/blog/ram-timings-cas-trcd-trp/.description: At the same 6000 MT/s transfer rate, CL30 corresponds to a calculated 10 ns CAS interval and CL36 to 12 ns. That 2 ns difference is useful specification arithmetic. It is not a measured gaming advantage, a full-system latency result or proof that either profile works on your motherboard.

image.alt: Decision diagram for DDR5-6000 CL30 vs CL36: what the 2 ns calculation can tell you

/blog/nvme-vs-sata-ssd-for-gaming/.title: Samsung 990 PRO 1 TB vs 870 EVO 1 TB: choose the supported interface
/blog/nvme-vs-sata-ssd-for-gaming/.description: The 990 PRO 1 TB is an M.2 PCIe/NVMe drive; the 870 EVO 1 TB is a 2.5-inch SATA drive. Choose the model your actual machine can connect and mount, then evaluate the workload and complete cost. Matching capacity does not make these physically or electrically interchangeable.

image.alt: Decision diagram for Samsung 990 PRO 1 TB vs 870 EVO 1 TB: choose the supported interface

/blog/am4-upgrade-vs-platform-replacemen.title: AM4 CPU upgrade or AM5 replacement? Compare the whole platform
/blog/am4-upgrade-vs-platform-replacemen.description: An AM4 drop-in candidate can preserve a supported board and DDR4 kit; an AM5 route changes the platform and requires DDR5. Compare complete supported configurations, including keeping the current PC. The CPU price alone cannot establish the cost or usefulness of either upgrade.

image.alt: Decision diagram for AM4 CPU upgrade or AM5 replacement? Compare the whole platform

/blog/new-pc-first-boot-setup-checklist/.title: First boot for a new PC: a safe checklist from power-on to a working baseline
/blog/new-pc-first-boot-setup-checklist/.description: Before installing software or enabling performance profiles, establish that the machine starts, recognizes the intended components and uses a documented configuration. Keep the exact manuals and a short observation log. First boot is a verification sequence, not a race to change every BIOS option.

image.alt: Decision diagram for First boot for a new PC: a safe checklist from power-on to a working baseline

/blog/check-cpu-bios-support/.title: Check CPU and BIOS support: exact model, minimum version and update method
/blog/check-cpu-bios-support/.description: A shared socket is one requirement. Before ordering a CPU, find the exact motherboard support entry, minimum firmware version and a supported way to obtain it. Unknown shipped BIOS is still unknown; an update method available on one board does not establish that another board can use it.

image.alt: Decision diagram for Check CPU and BIOS support: exact model, minimum version and update method

/blog/phased-pc-upgrade-plan/.title: Plan a phased PC upgrade: make every intermediate build usable
/blog/phased-pc-upgrade-plan/.description: Buying in stages works only when each intermediate configuration can perform the tasks you still need. Group dependent CPU, board and memory changes, preserve recovery and support evidence, and recheck each later purchase. A future shopping list is not proof that the machine will work between purchases.

image.alt: Decision diagram for Plan a phased PC upgrade: make every intermediate build usable

/blog/choose-a-pc-power-supply/.title: Choose a PC power supply: wattage, connectors, fit and the correct cables
/blog/choose-a-pc-power-supply/.description: A wattage label is one requirement, not a complete PSU selection. Check the whole system, exact component connection instructions, physical layout and manufacturer-approved modular cables. Preserve unknowns; matching plugs or a plausible 3D scene do not establish a safe installation.

image.alt: Decision diagram for Choose a PC power supply: wattage, connectors, fit and the correct cables
